jurisdiction.name: China
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: China governs AI through a dense layer of binding departmental rules rather than a single AI law. The Cyberspace Administration of China leads, with rules on algorithmic recommendation (2021), deep synthesis (2022), generative AI services (2023), labelling of AI-generated content (2025, backed by the mandatory national standard GB 45438-2025) and anthropomorphic AI interaction services (2026), all enforced through mandatory algorithm and generative-AI filing registers. These sit on the Cybersecurity Law, which since 1 January 2026 contains an AI article, the Data Security Law and the Personal Information Protection Law's rules on automated decision-making. Industrial policy runs through the State Council's 2017 New Generation AI Development Plan and the 2025 'AI+' initiative, with sector plans from MIIT, NDRC, the central bank and financial regulator, health, education and transport authorities, and an ethics-review regime for AI research (2023, extended by the 2026 AI ethics review measures). TC260 standards, including the AI Safety Governance Framework now in its third version, provide the technical layer. Shanghai and Shenzhen have local AI regulations, and Beijing, Guangdong, Zhejiang and other provinces issue AI action plans. A national AI law has been on the State Council's legislative plans since 2023 but no draft has been published.
lead_institutions: Cyberspace Administration of China (Office of the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission)
National People's Congress and its Standing Committee
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
National Technical Committee 260 on Cybersecurity (TC260) / Standardization Administration of China
People's Bank of China and National Financial Regulatory Administration
Provincial and municipal governments (Shanghai, Shenzhen, Beijing, Guangdong, Zhejiang)
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 7 October 2026, covering national laws and State Council measures, the Cyberspace Administration of China's rules and filing registers, national and TC260 standards, ministries and sector regulators, and provinces and cities including Shanghai, Shenzhen, Beijing, Guangdong and Zhejiang. Searches were made in Chinese and English. The websites of the health commission, the medical products administration and the commerce ministry, several provincial and city portals (Zhejiang, Hangzhou, Sichuan, Chongqing, Anhui, Hubei) and the Shanghai and Beijing people's congresses could not be read automatically; records from those sources are marked as located but not fully read, and the full texts of eleven national standards are still to be read. Pending: a national AI law (on the legislative plan, no draft published), Beijing's and Jiangsu's draft AI regulations, Hangzhou's robotics regulation, AI medical-device guidance and several school AI guides. Hong Kong and Macao are separate jurisdictions and are not covered here; no AI documents from them came up in this review.

instruments.official_title: 国务院关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见
instruments.english_title: Opinions of the State Council on Deepening the Implementation of the 'AI+' Initiative
instruments.issuing_authority: State Council
instruments.publisher_name: State Council
instruments.current_status: State Council opinions Guo Fa [2025] No. 11, dated 21 August 2025 and published on gov.cn 26 August 2025. The NDRC coordinates implementation. Current.
instruments.summary: State Council policy to integrate AI across science and technology, industry, consumption, livelihoods, governance and global cooperation, with targets of over 70% penetration of new intelligent terminals and AI agents by 2027 and over 90% by 2030, and an intelligent economy and society by 2035. On governance it calls for improving AI laws, regulations and ethics guidelines, advancing legislation on the healthy development of AI, optimising AI security assessment and filing systems, guarding against model black-box, hallucination and algorithmic-discrimination risks, and building AI monitoring, risk early-warning and emergency response systems under an inclusive, prudent, tiered approach.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current top-level national AI policy; the basis cited by later sectoral AI+ and government-AI guidance.

instruments.official_title: 人工智能科技伦理审查与服务办法（试行）
instruments.english_title: Measures for the Ethics Review and Services of Artificial Intelligence Science and Technology Activities (Trial)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; National Development and Reform Commission; Ministry of Education; Ministry of Science and Technology; Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs; National Health Commission; People's Bank of China; Cyberspace Administration of China; Chinese Academy of Sciences; China Association for Science and Technology
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: Issued under notice 工信部联科〔2026〕75号 by MIIT and nine other bodies; the notice is signed 20 March 2026 (the page metadata gives 成文日期 30 March 2026) and was published on miit.gov.cn on 2 April 2026. Art. 37: in force from the date of issue (自印发之日起施行); classified by MIIT as an administrative normative document (行政规范性文件). Implements MOST's 2023 Measures for S&T Ethics Review (Trial).
instruments.summary: AI-specific implementing rules under the 2023 S&T Ethics Review Measures: universities, research institutes, medical institutions and companies doing AI research and development that may raise ethics risks must set up AI S&T ethics committees, or use specialised AI ethics review and service centres. Applications must include the algorithm mechanism, data sources, testing methods and a risk assessment. Annexed list of AI activities that need expert re-review: human-machine fusion systems with strong effects on behaviour, emotions or health; algorithm models, apps and systems able to mobilise public opinion or shape social consciousness; and highly autonomous automated decision systems in safety or health-risk settings. Activities already under deep synthesis, algorithm recommendation or generative AI filing or approval regimes can skip expert re-review.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National ministry or sector-regulator instrument shaping AI governance in China.

instruments.official_title: 政务领域人工智能大模型部署应用指引
instruments.english_title: Guidelines for the Deployment and Application of Large AI Models in Government Affairs
instruments.issuing_authority: Office of the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission (Cyberspace Administration of China); National Development and Reform Commission
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: Jointly issued by the Office of the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission and the NDRC; announced and published on the CAC website on 10 October 2025. The text describes itself as a working orientation and basic reference for government departments, to be adjusted dynamically. Current.
instruments.summary: Joint CAC–NDRC guidelines for government departments at all levels on deploying large AI models, listing 13 reference use cases across public services, social governance, office work and decision support. They require general-purpose uses to rely on market models already filed with the cyberspace authorities, centralised provincial deployment (county level and below should reuse higher-level models), a supporting-role-only position for models, risk notices and labelling of model outputs, content review against hallucinations, security testing before launch, log audits and strict secrecy rules barring classified information from non-classified models.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: China's main national rules for public-sector use of generative AI.

instruments.official_title: 关于加快招标投标领域人工智能推广应用的实施意见
instruments.english_title: Implementation Opinions on Accelerating the Promotion and Application of Artificial Intelligence in Bidding and Tendering
instruments.issuing_authority: National Development and Reform Commission; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development; Ministry of Transport; Ministry of Water Resources; Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs; Ministry of Commerce; State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council
instruments.publisher_name: National Development and Reform Commission
instruments.current_status: Issued as 发改法规〔2026〕195号, dated 6 February 2026, published on ndrc.gov.cn on 10 February 2026 (reposted in the State Council policy library on 18 February 2026). No effective date stated.
instruments.summary: Eight-ministry opinions under the State Council 'AI+' initiative that set out AI use cases across the whole bidding process: drafting and compliance-checking tender documents, bid self-checks, digital bid opening, expert selection, AI-assisted bid evaluation, award support, contract generation and detection of bid-rigging. Targets full coverage of key scenarios in some provinces by end-2026 and national roll-out by end-2027. Model outputs must stay advisory: they do not replace the judgement of tenderers, agents, bidders or evaluation experts or change their legal responsibility, and algorithm and model filing and security review must be carried out to guard against black-box, hallucination and algorithmic-discrimination risks.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National ministry or sector-regulator instrument shaping AI governance in China.

instruments.official_title: 智能体规范应用与创新发展实施意见
instruments.english_title: Implementation Opinions on the Standardized Application and Innovative Development of AI Agents
instruments.issuing_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China; National Development and Reform Commission; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: Published on cac.gov.cn on 8 May 2026; the accompanying CAC Q&A (same day) states it was jointly issued by CAC, NDRC and MIIT. The text sets policy tasks and states no effective date or penalties. The cac.gov.cn page carries no document number or signing date.
instruments.summary: Joint CAC–NDRC–MIIT policy opinions implementing the State Council 'AI+' opinions for AI agents (systems able to perceive, remember, decide, interact and act autonomously): 38 measures on technical foundations and standards (including an agent interconnection protocol and an exploratory agent registration platform with digital identity), safety red lines and 19 priority application scenarios. Governance measures include defining which decisions only users may take, keeping agent actions within user authorisation, tiered governance with filing, testing and product recall for agents in sensitive fields, compliance self-testing for low-risk uses, and an industry credit-rating mechanism.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: CAC-led national rule, policy or register shaping China's governance of algorithms, generative and agentic AI.

instruments.official_title: 中华人民共和国网络安全法
instruments.english_title: Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China (2016, amended 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
instruments.publisher_name: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
instruments.current_status: Adopted 7 November 2016, in force since 1 June 2017. Amended by the NPCSC Decision of 28 October 2025 (Presidential Order No. 61), which added Article 20 on artificial intelligence; the amendments apply from 1 January 2026. In force as amended.
instruments.summary: China's framework law on network security: it sets security obligations for network operators, the multi-level protection scheme, critical information infrastructure protection, network information security and data localisation duties. The 2025 amendment added Article 20, under which the state supports basic AI research and key technologies such as algorithms, builds training-data and computing infrastructure, improves AI ethics norms and strengthens AI risk monitoring, assessment and safety supervision; it also raised fines (up to RMB 10 million for serious harm) and widened extraterritorial reach.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national law with an express AI provision (Article 20, from 1 January 2026); base law for CAC algorithm, deep-synthesis and generative-AI rules.

instruments.official_title: 中华人民共和国数据安全法
instruments.english_title: Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China
instruments.issuing_authority: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
instruments.publisher_name: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
instruments.current_status: Adopted 10 June 2021 by the 29th session of the 13th NPCSC; in force since 1 September 2021 (Article 55).
instruments.summary: Basic law on data processing and data security: it creates national data classification and grading protection, a category of 'important data' with risk-assessment and reporting duties, a data security review regime and export controls on data. Article 28 requires that data processing and research into new data technologies benefit economic and social development and conform to social morality and ethics.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Governs the data used to train and operate AI systems; cited as a legal basis by China's generative-AI and network data rules.

instruments.official_title: 中华人民共和国个人信息保护法
instruments.english_title: Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China
instruments.issuing_authority: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
instruments.publisher_name: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
instruments.current_status: Adopted 20 August 2021 by the 30th session of the 13th NPCSC; in force since 1 November 2021 (Article 74).
instruments.summary: China's comprehensive personal information law, setting legal bases for processing, sensitive-data rules, cross-border transfer conditions, individuals' rights and processor duties, with the CAC coordinating enforcement. Article 24 requires automated decision-making to be transparent and fair, bars unreasonable differential treatment in prices and trading terms, requires a non-personalised option or easy opt-out for automated push marketing, and gives individuals a right to an explanation and to refuse decisions made solely by automated means that significantly affect their rights; Article 55 requires a prior personal information protection impact assessment for automated decision-making.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main statutory rules on automated decision-making and profiling that apply to AI systems.

instruments.official_title: 中华人民共和国科学技术进步法
instruments.english_title: Law of the People's Republic of China on Progress of Science and Technology (2021 revision)
instruments.issuing_authority: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
instruments.publisher_name: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
instruments.current_status: First adopted 2 July 1993, revised 2007; second comprehensive revision adopted 24 December 2021 by the 32nd session of the 13th NPCSC, in force since 1 January 2022 (Article 117). The law has no AI-specific article; it is recorded for its S&T ethics provisions.
instruments.summary: China's basic law on science and technology, revised in 2021 into 12 chapters and 117 articles covering basic research, technology transfer, national laboratories and S&T personnel. Article 103 sets up a national S&T ethics committee and requires research institutions, universities and enterprises to take responsibility for S&T ethics management and to carry out ethics review of S&T activities, and Article 107 prohibits research and application activities that violate S&T ethics.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Statutory basis for China's S&T ethics review system, which ministries apply to AI research and development (e.g. the AI ethics review measures).

instruments.official_title: 网络数据安全管理条例
instruments.english_title: Regulations on Network Data Security Management
instruments.issuing_authority: State Council
instruments.publisher_name: State Council
instruments.current_status: Administrative regulation promulgated by State Council Order No. 790, signed 24 September 2024 (adopted at the State Council executive meeting of 30 August 2024; released on gov.cn 30 September 2024); in force since 1 January 2025.
instruments.summary: State Council regulation implementing the Cybersecurity, Data Security and Personal Information Protection Laws for network data, covering personal information, important data, cross-border transfers and large platform duties. Article 19 requires providers of generative AI services to strengthen security management of training data and training-data processing and to prevent and handle network data security risks, and Article 42 requires platforms that push information by automated decision-making to offer an easy-to-use option to switch off personalised recommendations and delete personal-feature labels.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding regulation with explicit generative-AI training-data and recommender-system duties.

instruments.official_title: 未成年人网络保护条例
instruments.english_title: Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online
instruments.issuing_authority: State Council
instruments.publisher_name: State Council
instruments.current_status: Administrative regulation promulgated by State Council Order No. 766 of 16 October 2023 (adopted 20 September 2023); in force since 1 January 2024.
instruments.summary: State Council regulation on minors' online protection, covering online literacy, content standards, personal information and prevention of internet addiction, with the CAC coordinating. It prohibits network product and service providers from using automated decision-making for commercial marketing to minors (Article 24) and requires them to optimise algorithm models and combine AI, big data and human review to detect cyberbullying content (Article 26).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on algorithmic and automated decision-making systems in services used by minors.

instruments.official_title: 新一代人工智能发展规划
instruments.english_title: New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan
instruments.issuing_authority: State Council
instruments.publisher_name: State Council
instruments.current_status: Issued by the State Council notice Guo Fa [2017] No. 35, dated 8 July 2017 and published 20 July 2017. Sets targets to 2020, 2025 and 2030; not formally superseded (the 2025 'AI+' opinions build on it).
instruments.summary: China's national AI strategy, setting three steps: keep pace with leading AI technology by 2020, achieve major breakthroughs by 2025 and become the world's primary AI innovation centre by 2030, with core AI industry targets for each stage. It calls for initial AI laws, ethical norms and policies by 2025, with AI safety assessment and control capabilities, and assigns tasks on R&D, the smart economy, smart society, military-civil fusion and infrastructure.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding national AI strategy; source of the national AI governance committee and the 2025 target for AI laws and ethics.

instruments.official_title: 关于加强科技伦理治理的意见
instruments.english_title: Opinions on Strengthening the Governance of Science and Technology Ethics
instruments.issuing_authority: General Office of the CPC Central Committee; General Office of the State Council
instruments.publisher_name: General Office of the CPC Central Committee
instruments.current_status: Issued jointly by the two General Offices and published in full on gov.cn on 20 March 2022. Current.
instruments.summary: Central opinions setting up China's S&T ethics governance system, with a National S&T Ethics Committee and the Ministry of Science and Technology as its secretariat. Units engaged in life sciences, medicine or artificial intelligence whose research touches ethically sensitive areas must establish S&T ethics (review) committees, and the opinions call for ethics norms and guidelines for AI and other priority fields and for research on S&T ethics legislation for AI during the 14th Five-Year Plan period.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Policy basis for mandatory ethics review of AI research and for the AI ethics review measures.

instruments.official_title: 新一代人工智能治理原则——发展负责任的人工智能
instruments.english_title: Governance Principles for New Generation AI: Developing Responsible Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: National New Generation Artificial Intelligence Governance Expert Committee (under the Ministry of Science and Technology)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science and Technology
instruments.current_status: Released 17 June 2019; full text on most.gov.cn. Further detailed by the 2021 Ethical Norms for New Generation AI.
instruments.summary: China's first national set of AI governance principles, framed as 'responsible AI'. Its eight principles are harmony and friendliness, fairness and justice, inclusiveness and sharing, respect for privacy, security and controllability, shared responsibility, open collaboration, and agile governance. It calls for AI systems to become auditable, supervisable, traceable and trustworthy, and for accountability mechanisms covering developers and users.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National ministry or sector-regulator instrument shaping AI governance in China.

instruments.official_title: 新一代人工智能伦理规范
instruments.english_title: Ethical Norms for New Generation Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: National New Generation Artificial Intelligence Governance Expert Committee (under the Ministry of Science and Technology)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science and Technology
instruments.current_status: Released by the committee on 25 September 2021; full text published on most.gov.cn on 26 September 2021. Refines the 2019 Governance Principles.
instruments.summary: Ethics code for everyone engaged in AI management, research and development, supply and use. It sets six basic norms (enhance human well-being, promote fairness and justice, protect privacy and security, ensure controllability and trustworthiness, strengthen accountability, improve ethical literacy) and 18 specific norms for management, R&D, supply and use. Examples: avoid data and algorithm bias, tell users when a product uses AI and state its functions and limits, respect the right not to use AI, and forbid illegal or harmful uses of AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National ministry or sector-regulator instrument shaping AI governance in China.

instruments.official_title: 全球人工智能治理倡议
instruments.english_title: Global AI Governance Initiative
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of the People's Republic of China (published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
instruments.current_status: Released 18 October 2023 (date of the CAC publication; announced at the third Belt and Road Forum); the MFA statements page carries the full text dated 20 October 2023. A unilateral Chinese policy initiative, not a treaty.
instruments.summary: China's international position on AI governance, covering development, security and governance. It calls for a people-centred approach and 'AI for good', respect for other countries' sovereignty and laws, opposition to using AI to manipulate public opinion or interfere in other countries' affairs, prudent and responsible military AI, tiered risk-based management with testing and assessment, data and privacy protection, and a greater voice for developing countries, and supports discussions within the UN framework on an international AI governance body.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: China's main international AI governance policy statement.

instruments.official_title: 人工智能全球治理行动计划
instruments.english_title: Global AI Governance Action Plan
instruments.issuing_authority: 2025 World Artificial Intelligence Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance (published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
instruments.current_status: Issued 26 July 2025 at the 2025 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in Shanghai; full text published by the MFA the same day. A non-binding action plan, not a treaty.
instruments.summary: A 13-point action plan, published by China, calling on governments, international organisations, companies and others to cooperate on AI under principles of AI for good, respect for sovereignty, development orientation, safety and controllability, fairness and openness. Its points cover innovation, AI across sectors, digital infrastructure, open source, high-quality data, energy and environment, standards, public-sector use, AI safety governance with risk testing and assessment, implementation of the UN Global Digital Compact, capacity building and inclusive multi-stakeholder governance, and it supports the UN international scientific panel on AI and global dialogue on AI governance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: China's current international AI governance programme.

instruments.official_title: 互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定
instruments.english_title: Provisions on the Administration of Algorithmic Recommendation for Internet Information Services
instruments.issuing_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; Ministry of Public Security; State Administration for Market Regulation
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: CAC Order No. 9, adopted at the CAC office meeting of 16 November 2021, signed 31 December 2021 by CAC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR; in force since 1 March 2022. Posted on cac.gov.cn on 4 January 2022.
instruments.summary: Departmental rule governing services that use algorithmic recommendation technologies (generation/synthesis, personalised push, ranking and selection, search filtering, scheduling and decision-making) to provide information in China. Providers must set up algorithm review, ethics review and security management, publish the basic principles of their recommendation services, let users switch off personalisation and delete tags, and protect minors, the elderly, gig workers and consumers (no price discrimination). Providers with public-opinion attributes or social mobilisation capacity must file their algorithms with CAC within ten working days of starting service and carry out security assessments.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: CAC-led national rule, policy or register shaping China's governance of algorithms, generative and agentic AI.

instruments.official_title: 互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定
instruments.english_title: Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis of Internet Information Services
instruments.issuing_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; Ministry of Public Security
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: CAC Order No. 12, adopted 3 November 2022, signed 25 November 2022 by CAC, MIIT and MPS; in force since 10 January 2023. Posted on cac.gov.cn on 11 December 2022.
instruments.summary: Departmental rule covering deep synthesis services (text, voice, music, face generation/swap, image and video generation, 3D and virtual scenes) offered in China, binding service providers, technical supporters and users. Providers must verify users' real identities, review inputs and outputs, manage training data, obtain consent before editing others' biometric information, and add labels; content that may confuse or mislead the public must carry a conspicuous label. Providers with public-opinion attributes or social mobilisation capacity, and technical supporters, must complete algorithm filing, and new models or functions that generate biometric or sensitive content require a security assessment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: CAC-led national rule, policy or register shaping China's governance of algorithms, generative and agentic AI.

instruments.official_title: 生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法
instruments.english_title: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
instruments.issuing_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China; National Development and Reform Commission; Ministry of Education; Ministry of Science and Technology; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; Ministry of Public Security; National Radio and Television Administration
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: CAC Order No. 15, adopted 23 May 2023, signed 10 July 2023 by seven departments; in force since 15 August 2023. Posted on cac.gov.cn on 13 July 2023.
instruments.summary: Departmental rule for generative AI services offered to the public in China (text, images, audio, video), applying inclusive-prudent and tiered supervision; research and internal use not offered to the public are excluded. Providers bear content-producer responsibility: lawful training data and models, respect for IP and personal information, measures against discrimination, labelling under the deep synthesis rules, user complaint channels and protections against minors' over-reliance. Services with public-opinion attributes or social mobilisation capacity must undergo a security assessment and algorithm filing.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: CAC-led national rule, policy or register shaping China's governance of algorithms, generative and agentic AI.

instruments.official_title: 人工智能生成合成内容标识办法
instruments.english_title: Measures for Labeling Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Synthesized Content
instruments.issuing_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; Ministry of Public Security; National Radio and Television Administration
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: Issued by notice Guoxinban Tongzi [2025] No. 2 dated 7 March 2025 (posted on cac.gov.cn 14 March 2025) to provincial cyberspace, telecoms, public security and broadcasting authorities for implementation; in force since 1 September 2025. Issued as a normative document under the three CAC departmental rules, not as a numbered departmental rule. Art. 11 links to mandatory national standards (the companion labelling standard is recorded by the standards part).
instruments.summary: Sets labelling obligations for providers covered by the algorithm recommendation, deep synthesis and generative AI rules: explicit labels (text, audio prompts, visible marks on images, video and virtual scenes) and implicit labels (metadata identifying the provider and content ID) for AI-generated or synthesised content. Content distribution platforms must detect implicit labels and add prominent notices for confirmed, possible or suspected AI content; app stores must check labelling materials when listing AI apps. Providers may supply unlabelled content only under user agreements with six-month log retention, and no one may maliciously remove, alter or forge labels.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: CAC-led national rule, policy or register shaping China's governance of algorithms, generative and agentic AI.

instruments.official_title: 人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法
instruments.english_title: Interim Measures for the Administration of Anthropomorphic Interactive Services Based on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China; National Development and Reform Commission; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology; Ministry of Public Security; State Administration for Market Regulation
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: CAC Order No. 21, adopted at the CAC office meeting of 2 February 2026, signed 10 April 2026 by CAC, NDRC, MIIT, MPS and SAMR; in force since 15 July 2026. Supersedes the December 2025 consultation draft.
instruments.summary: Departmental rule for AI services that simulate human personality and offer sustained emotional interaction (companionship, emotional care and support); customer service, Q&A, work, education and research assistants without sustained emotional interaction are excluded. Providers must not foster emotional dependence or manipulate users, must intervene and contact guardians or emergency contacts in self-harm or crisis situations, remind users every two hours, tell users they are interacting with AI, offer easy exit, and may not train on sensitive interaction data without separate consent. Virtual partner or relative services for minors are banned, a minors' mode and parental controls are required, and a security assessment must be filed with the provincial CAC at launch or above 1 million registered or 100,000 monthly active users; fines of up to RMB 200,000 apply.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: CAC-led national rule, policy or register shaping China's governance of algorithms, generative and agentic AI.

instruments.official_title: 人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法（征求意见稿）
instruments.english_title: Interim Measures for the Administration of Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services (Draft for Comment)
instruments.issuing_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: Released by CAC for public comment on 27 December 2025; comments closed 25 January 2026. Superseded by the final measures (CAC Order No. 21, 10 April 2026).
instruments.summary: CAC consultation draft of rules for AI products or services that simulate human personality and interact emotionally with people. It proposed tiered supervision, duties to prevent addiction and dependence, crisis intervention, minors' and elderly users' protections, security assessments and algorithm filing. The final measures narrowed the scope to sustained emotional-interaction services and added co-issuers and fines.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: CAC-led national rule, policy or register shaping China's governance of algorithms, generative and agentic AI.

instruments.official_title: 数字虚拟人信息服务管理办法（征求意见稿）
instruments.english_title: Measures for the Administration of Digital Virtual Human Information Services (Draft for Comment)
instruments.issuing_authority: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.publisher_name: Cyberspace Administration of China
instruments.current_status: Released by CAC for public comment on 3 April 2026; comments closed 6 May 2026. No final version found on cac.gov.cn as of 7 October 2026; effective date left blank in the draft.

organizations.name: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress
organizations.ai_governance_role: Permanent body of the national legislature; enacts and amends national laws, including the Cybersecurity, Data Security, Personal Information Protection and Science and Technology Progress Laws, and sets the annual legislative plan that lists AI legislation.

organizations.name: State Council
organizations.ai_governance_role: Central government; issues administrative regulations and national AI policy, including the 2017 New Generation AI Development Plan and the 2025 'AI+' opinions.

organizations.name: Cyberspace Administration of China
organizations.ai_governance_role: National internet regulator (one institution with the Office of the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission). Lead issuer of China's algorithm, deep synthesis, generative AI, AI content labelling and anthropomorphic AI rules; runs the algorithm filing system and generative AI service filing.

organizations.name: National Development and Reform Commission
organizations.ai_governance_role: Macro-planning commission; leads the State Council 'AI+' initiative drafting and issues AI rules for bidding and tendering.

organizations.name: General Office of the CPC Central Committee
organizations.ai_governance_role: Party central office that co-issues national policy opinions with the State Council General Office, including the 2022 opinions on S&T ethics governance.

organizations.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
organizations.ai_governance_role: Publishes China's international AI governance positions, including the Global AI Governance Initiative and the Global AI Governance Action Plan.

organizations.name: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
organizations.ai_governance_role: Lead ministry for the AI industry: issues AI industrial policy, AI standardisation guides, humanoid-robot and AI+manufacturing plans, and the 2026 AI S&T ethics review measures.

organizations.name: State Administration for Market Regulation
organizations.ai_governance_role: Market regulator: platform pricing and antitrust rules that address algorithmic price discrimination and algorithmic collusion.

organizations.name: Ministry of Science and Technology
